segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.

and he gave him allowances that were sufficient for him.
Now this 'Abd al-Rahman was the son of one of the slaves of the slain Caliph al-Musta'sim,
a Roman (Greek) by race.
And when Baghdad was taken,
he was saved from slaughter,
and came to Mosul,
and sat in the market doing carpentry,
because he loved it and had learned it.
And he went to the fortress of 'Imadiyah,
and said to 'Izz al-Din, the lord of the fortress,
that he was able to perform wondrous works,
which he had learned by revelation from spiritual beings.
And this 'Izz al-Din brought him to the King of Kings, Abaqa.
And when he conversed with the king, he said:
"Let them bring me (or: Bring me {OCR?}) into the fortress of Tela (al-Tall),
where your treasury is,
so that I may show you my craft."
And when they brought him there,
he began measuring the ground on this side and on that.
And at last he stopped in one place,
and commanded that they should dig there,
while he stood at a distance.
And when they dug,
they found a ring wherein was a seal that was very wondrous and precious;
and they took it and brought it to the king.
And when in this single matter his word was verified,
they believed everything that he said,
namely that he was able to cast out demons
and to understand the mysteries of the devils.
And he gained great boldness of speech among the royal princes,
to such a degree that even the entire administration of the kingdom was committed to him,
especially in the brief time in which Ahmad reigned.
It is said
that when the Tatars pillaged the treasury of the Caliph,
they also took him as a captive,
and brought him with them to the fortress of Tela,
and he used to enter the fortress carrying things;
and that ring which he found,
he himself had buried it in that place.
And in the Latter Kanun (January) of this year,
Arghun, the King of Kings, sent yarlighs (edicts) to all the countries, saying:
"Because Ahmad departed from the laws of our fathers,
and walked in the way of the Arabs (Islam),
which our fathers did not know,
all the royal princes agreed together,
and cast him out from the kingdom,
and sent him to the Great Khan, our father, so that he might judge him.
And me they have seated upon the throne of the kingdom,
from the Gihon (Oxus) as far as Frankland.
Therefore, be of good cheer,
and let each person attend to his own business.
And let the governors and rulers in every place not"
